column2: Zen sand table (a Sisyphus kinetic sand table seen from above). A polished steel ball, pulled by a hidden magnet, ploughs grooves through fine sand; the panel is the sand, lit by one low raking lamp so every groove is a real relief: a bright lit wall, a dark shadowed wall, glittering grains. The time is ploughed as continuous single-line groove script (each digit one unbroken path, like the ball would draw it), designed as a font for a ball that cannot lift. Always alive: the ball keeps drawing a slow decorative border spiral or rose; the lamp drifts round with the time of day, so the relief shading turns. Minute turn: the ball travels to the changing digit, smooths it away with tight back-and-forth sweeps (the sand visibly flattening), then draws the new one stroke by stroke. Hour: the classic full-table spiral wipe from the outside in, the ball racing, then it ploughs the time back. The owner loved 'sand': smooth, physical, hypnotic is the point.

Starling murmuration at dusk. Several thousand birds (sub-pixel dots, coverage-rendered, dark against a glowing dusk sky that follows the real time of day: amber, rose, violet, deep blue with a moon at night) fly as one living cloud with real boids-like flocking (smooth, deterministic: e.g. birds attracted to target points that slide, plus curl-noise wander). The flock's density forms the digits: the time is written in birds, the letterforms soft, swelling and breathing, edges ragged with stragglers. A reed bed or a city skyline silhouette at the bottom. Minute turn: the changing digit's birds peel off in a swirling ribbon, loop over the sky and pour into the new shape. Hour: a peregrine falcon dives through; the whole flock explodes into a shimmering wave (the famous ripple of density) and regathers into the time. The density field must still read as numbers at rest from 2 m.

Domino run. An isometric 3D tabletop (real perspective or isometric projection, shaded faces, soft shadows, a warm lamp): the time is laid out as lines of standing dominoes, ivory with black pips catching specular light, each digit one continuous domino trail (letterforms for a trail, like a domino artist would design them). Always alive: a slow camera orbit or drift, a tiny wind-up robot (or the owner's rainbow frog in round glasses, small but 6+ px) walks around setting up stray dominoes. Minute turn: a domino at the start of the changing digit is flicked and the whole digit topples in a chain wave (real angular motion, each domino rotating about its edge and leaning on the next), clattering flat; then the trail of the new digit tips back up in reverse, like a rewound film, or the robot sets it up in a fast stop-motion run. Hour: one giant chain runs through all four digits and a spiral, with a bell at the end. Satisfying physics.

Gear train. The digits are built of meshing brass and steel gears: each digit a chain of interlocking spur gears laid along its strokes, every gear turning (adjacent gears counter-rotate at speeds set by their tooth counts: get the kinematics right, it is what makes it hypnotic), with anti-aliased teeth, specular glints sweeping round the rims, axle screws, a dark machined backplate with a faint engraved pattern. A visible drive: one motor gear or an escapement with a swinging balance wheel ticks the seconds and drives everything. Minute turn: the changing digit's gears disengage, lift off, roll along their neighbours like planets and re-mesh into the new digit's arrangement (the gear train is never broken visually: they roll, they don't teleport). Hour: a chime train engages, a big wheel sweeps across, every gear speeds up and slows. Design gear-chain letterforms that read at 2 m.

Frogzilla. A night city skyline at the harbour, the time spelled by the skyline itself: four Art Deco skyscraper groups whose silhouettes and lit windows ARE the digits (design architecture letterforms: setbacks, spires, antennae with blinking red lights). Behind them in the harbour wades a giant kaiju: the owner's avatar, a rainbow frog in round glasses, enormous and cute (30+ px tall), with parallax water, searchlights sweeping the clouds, a tiny helicopter, reflections on the water. Always alive: the frog breathes, blinks behind its glasses, looks around, the city twinkles, traffic streams. Minute turn: the frog 'accidentally' leans on the changing digit's tower; it crumbles in a dust cloud (falling debris physics), then a time-lapse of tiny cranes rebuilds the new digit floor by floor (partly built must never read as a different number). Hour: the frog roars a rainbow beam into the sky that lights up the clouds and briefly the whole city, then sheepishly pushes up its glasses. Charm first.

Soap bubbles. Soap-film bubbles with real thin-film interference colour (the iridescence comes from film thickness: swirling bands of magenta, gold, cyan, green that drift and drain downward over time, the top thinning to black just before a pop), each with a bright specular window highlight and a rim. The time is a foam: clusters of bubbles packed into each digit, with the Plateau-law geometry of real foam where bubbles meet (flat shared walls, 120-degree junctions). Always alive: films swirl, small bubbles drift up and wobble, gentle bobbing. Minute turn: the changing digit's bubbles pop in a chain reaction (each pop a fast ring of droplets, the film snapping back), and a bubble wand at the edge blows a stream of new bubbles that drift in, jostle and pack into the new digit. Hour: one giant bubble blown across the whole panel, its swirling film showing the time reflected inside, then it pops and showers. Colour is the wow here.

Skywriter. A vintage biplane writes the time in smoke across a sky that follows the real time of day (dawn, blue noon with drifting cumulus, sunset, night with stars, moon and the plane's navigation lights). The smoke is a soft fluid trail that slowly billows, diffuses and drifts with the wind, so letterforms are cursive smoke script, written in one continuous stroke per digit as a pilot would fly it (design that script). Always alive: the plane loops lazily between jobs, the smoke breathes and curls, birds, clouds. Minute turn: the wind blows the changing digit away into wisps, and the plane banks in, re-writes the new digit with the smoke puffing out (real plane motion: banking, nose following the path). Hour: an aerobatic team of three planes with coloured smoke writes the hour with loops and a heart, the old smoke dispersing. Smoke must stay legible: refresh and thicken it. Make the plane big enough (10+ px) to be a character.

Maze chase. A neon arcade maze whose walls ARE the digits: the time is drawn as double-line glowing maze walls (rounded corners like the 1980 classic), designed as maze letterforms you could actually run through. The hero is the owner's rainbow frog in round glasses (8-10 px, original character, not Pac-Man), hopping through the corridors and catching flies (the dots) with its tongue, chased by four little ghost-like beetles with personalities. Real pathfinding along the maze, smooth sub-pixel movement, mouth/tongue animation. Minute turn: the frog eats a power fly, the beetles turn blue and flee, and the changing digit's walls slide like a sliding-tile puzzle into the new digit's walls (walls never vanish: they glide). Hour: LEVEL UP: the maze flashes, the frog does a victory dance, a fruit bonus with the hour, and the colours of the walls change for the new level. A game the owner would watch for minutes.
